cards.text: Israel is out in the wilderness. And one day, somebody finds a man gathering wood. On the Sabbath day.

cards.question: The people who found the man gathering wood on the Sabbath bring him to someone. Who?

answers.text: Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation
Joshua and Caleb and the elders
Eleazar and the priests at the tabernacle

cards.text: Here's the snag, friend. Nobody's been told yet what should be done to him.

cards.question: Until they know what to do with the man, they place him in ___.

cards.text: So the man waits, and I know a little something about waiting in the dark while somebody else decides what happens to you. Then the LORD speaks to Moses about him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses must happen to the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath?

answers.text: He must surely be put to death
He must bring a sin offering
He must stay outside the camp seven days

cards.question: The LORD says only Moses and Aaron are to stone the man.

cards.text: This one's heavy, friend. The whole congregation takes the man outside the camp and stones him to death.

cards.question: The congregation does this just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and this time it's about what the Israelites wear. I've worn the same apron every single day since I got here, so believe me, I am LISTENING.

cards.question: What does God tell the Israelites to make for the corners of their garments?
On each of the tassels for their garments goes a ___ cord.
The tassels are only for the generation out in the wilderness.

cards.text: These tassels aren't just for looks, friend. God says they're for the Israelites to look at, like a string tied around your finger, and me? I'd need one on every corner of this apron AND two on the mustache.

cards.question: When the Israelites look at their tassels, what are they supposed to remember?

answers.text: all the commandments of the LORD
the day they crossed the Red Sea
the names of the twelve tribes

cards.question: God says the tassels will help the Israelites follow their own heart and their own eyes.
God says when the Israelites remember and obey all His commandments, they will be ___ to their God.
Then God reminds Israel who He is. What does He say He did for them?

answers.text: brought them out of the land of Egypt
led them across the Jordan River
gave them the city of Jericho

cards.text: And He ends right where He started: "I am the LORD your God." He says it twice in one verse, and when God repeats Himself, I've learned to put down the dough and pay attention.

findings.problem: The question says "The congregation does this," and "this" points back to the stoning on card 8, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the congregation does, for example that they take the man outside the camp and stone him.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the cord's color (blue, scarlet or purple). Nothing earlier lets them reason it out, so it tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning. It works like the Psalm 23 "oil, myrrh or perfume" example of guessing a detail. It also comes right after card 11, another discovery question, with no story card between them.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card runs past 2 sentences, because "and me?" breaks off as its own question. It also packs three things into one card: the tassels' purpose, the string-around-the-finger comparison and the apron and mustache joke. It should be split or trimmed to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer, "all the commandments of the LORD," uses scripture wording ("of the LORD"). The wrong answers, "the day they crossed the Red Sea" and "the names of the twelve tribes," are plain. That difference makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
